$comment: Sources catalog. Every non-exact data value references a source id here (enforced by validate-data.ts). ids are kebab-case. Unit-definition sources (Engine seed) PLUS fuel-property / emission-factor sources (Data agent, from docs/research-notes.md §2). retrieved_at is the date the Research/Data agent fetched the page (2026-07-04 for this pass). Reliability + license notes are verbatim from the research pass; see docs/research-notes.md §2/§5 for the full provenance discussion.

sources.title: Universal Converter — Conversion Rules (docs/conversion-rules.md)
sources.reliability: Normative project rulebook; records the definitional conventions (IT calorie/BTU, toe/tce/boe, therm, Julian year) v0.1 adopts. Used as a source_ref only for the project's chosen conventions where an external primary citation is also attached (nist-sp811 / iea-unit-conventions).
sources.notes: This is not an independent external authority — it is our own internal document recording which convention we chose to follow, alongside a pointer to the real external source. We keep it listed together with that external source wherever it applies.

sources.title: Guide for the Use of the International System of Units (SI), NIST Special Publication 811 (2008 edition)
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), US Dept. of Commerce
sources.license: US federal government work — public domain, freely citable and reusable
sources.reliability: Very high — the canonical US reference for SI usage and exact conversion factors. Defines BTU_IT (1.05505585262 kJ), cal_IT (4.1868 J), cal_th (4.184 J), the avoirdupois pound, US/imperial gallon and cubic foot. 2008 edition not yet updated for the 2019 SI redefinition (NIST's own note), which does not affect the mechanical conversion factors used here.
sources.notes: Appendix B lists the exact conversion factors used for lb, gallons, ft^3, cal_IT and BTU_IT. DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.811e2008. PDF mirror: https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/pdf/sp811.pdf

sources.title: IEA Unit Converter (Data Tools) — energy-sector unit conventions (toe, tce)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (the tool/page itself) — reusable with attribution. Distinct from IEA's paywalled statistical data products.
sources.reliability: Medium-high for definitions (toe = 41.868 GJ net; tce = 29.3076 GJ). Tool last updated 30 Dec 2023. Shows no per-factor sourcing itself, so used only for the standard-definition energy-equivalence conventions.
sources.notes: The widely-cited IEA/UN conventions are: 1 toe = 41.868 GJ (derived from 10⁷ kilocalories, International Table definition, net basis), and 1 tce = 29.3076 GJ (7 gigacalories, IT). The IEA's 'World Energy Balances' dataset, which has detailed country-level data, sits behind a paywall and is not used as a numeric source here.

sources.title: 2025 Government GHG Conversion Factors for Company Reporting (Full Set)
sources.publisher: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
sources.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 — explicit permission for commercial AND non-commercial reuse, adaptation and redistribution, with attribution ('Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0').
sources.reliability: Very high — the single most valuable fuel source for this project: per-fuel density, NCV/GCV, CO2/CH4/N2O split and derived CO2e in one authoritative, actively maintained, licensing-friendly dataset. Data year 2025; next publication June 2026.
sources.notes: Full data set (Excel): https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6846a4f55e92539572806125/ghg-conversion-factors-2025-full-set.xlsx . Fuel values were taken from its 'Fuels', 'Bioenergy', 'Fuel properties', 'UK electricity' and 'Outside of scopes' sheets. This is used as the general-purpose, UK-context default source.

sources.title: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 2 (Energy), Ch.1 & Ch.2
sources.publisher: IPCC / Institute for Global Environmental Strategies (IGES)
sources.license: © IPCC 2006. Free reuse of short excerpts / individual default values with full attribution is authorized; bulk verbatim republication of full tables requires written permission. This catalog cites only the specific fuel rows it uses, each with its citation.
sources.reliability: Very high — the global Tier-1 default fallback for net calorific values (Vol.2 Ch.1 Table 1.2) and default CO2 emission factors (Vol.2 Ch.2 Table 2.2) when no better regional source exists. Used here as primary for crude oil, anthracite and lignite (rank-based, global), which DESNZ does not cover cleanly.
sources.notes: Ch.1 (NCV): https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/pdf/2_Volume2/V2_1_Ch1_Introduction.pdf ; Ch.2 (EF): https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/pdf/2_Volume2/V2_2_Ch2_Stationary_Combustion.pdf . Factors are in kg/TJ and NCVs in TJ/Gg (= GJ/tonne). 95% CI ranges recorded where given.

sources.title: Energy units & calculators explained; Energy conversion calculators; CO2 emission coefficients
sources.license: US federal government work — public domain
sources.reliability: High — the standard US-specific cross-check for heat contents and CO2 coefficients. Heat-content data year varies by table (Monthly Energy Review Appendix A, annual); CO2 coefficients based on 2022 data, used for 2023+ estimates; page release date 2024-09-18.
sources.notes: CO2 coefficients: https://www.eia.gov/environment/emissions/co2_vol_mass.php ; conversion calculators: https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/units-and-calculators/energy-conversion-calculators.php . Used only as a US cross-check figure in notes, never averaged with DESNZ/IPCC.

sources.title: GHG Emission Factors Hub (2025 edition)
sources.publisher: US EPA — Center for Corporate Climate Leadership
sources.license: US federal government work — public domain, freely reusable
sources.reliability: High — 435 factors, Scope 1/2/3, widely used for US corporate GHG reporting; stationary-combustion factors trace to 40 CFR Part 98 / EPA's GHG Inventory. Published Jan 2025 ('last modified 15 January 2025').
sources.notes: PDF: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2025-01/ghg-emission-factors-hub-2025.pdf ; XLSX: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/other-files/2025-01/ghg-emission-factors-hub-2025.xlsx . Table 6 holds eGRID electricity factors (US average). US-specific cross-check only in v0.1.

sources.title: Hydrogen Tools — Lower and Higher Heating Values of Hydrogen and Other Fuels; Basic Hydrogen Properties Chart
sources.publisher: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) for the US DOE Hydrogen Safety Panel / H2tools.org
sources.license: US DOE-funded public resource — citable with attribution
sources.reliability: High by reputation for hydrogen physical properties. The primary page still blocked automated fetch (HTTP 403) in the Data agent's follow-up pass. H2Tools republishes the DOE GREET / ORNL heating-value table; the fetchable primaries for these figures are that GREET/ORNL table and the NIST Chemistry WebBook (see nist-webbook). Values here are confirmed against those fetchable primaries, not recalled from memory.
sources.notes: Hydrogen: LHV 119.96 MJ/kg (~33.3 kWh/kg, NIST WebBook-traceable; DOE GREET gives 120.21), HHV 141.79 MJ/kg (~39.4 kWh/kg, NIST-printed; GREET gives 142.18), gas density 0.08988 kg/m³ at 0 °C/1 bar, liquid density 70.8 kg/m³ (NIST-precise 70.85) at boiling point (−252.87 °C). GREET/ORNL mirror: https://courses.grainger.illinois.edu/npre470/sp2018/web/Lower_and_Higher_Heating_Values_of_Gas_Liquid_and_Solid_Fuels.pdf ; basic properties chart: https://h2tools.org/basic-hydrogen-properties-chart

sources.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook, NIST Standard Reference Database Number 69
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), US Dept. of Commerce
sources.license: US federal government work — public domain, freely citable
sources.reliability: Very high — the authoritative US thermochemical reference. Used for the NIST-traceable hydrogen heating values (LHV 119.96, HHV 141.79 MJ/kg, from the 25 °C heat-of-combustion / formation enthalpies) and hydrogen density (gas 0.08988 kg/m³, liquid 70.85 kg/m³ via NIST 'Thermophysical Properties of Hydrogen').
sources.notes: Used as the primary citation for hydrogen properties, since the H2Tools page could not be fetched automatically. This was confirmed on 2026-07-04 against NIST heat-of-combustion and thermophysical-property tables, and cross-checked against the DOE GREET/ORNL data (see the h2tools entry) — small differences of about 0.2% were found and were not averaged together.

sources.title: Greenhouse gas emission intensity of electricity generation in Europe
sources.license: EEA content generally reusable with attribution (standard EU-institution practice); not explicitly re-verified on this page in the research pass.
sources.reliability: Medium — good EU-aggregate cross-check for electricity carbon intensity. EU-27 2023 value 242 gCO2/kWh (down from 292 in 2022). The exact 2024 figure was not extractable from the fetched page; the 2023 figure is used with an explicit year caveat.
sources.notes: Used only for the illustrative, region+year-labeled EU electricity example — never as a default factor.

sources.title: eGRID Summary Tables 2023
sources.publisher: US EPA — Emissions & Generation Resource Integrated Database (eGRID)
sources.license: US federal government work — public domain, freely reusable
sources.reliability: High — eGRID is the authoritative US inventory of power-plant emissions and generation, compiled from EPA CAMD, EIA and other federal reporting. This is the primary summary document (Rev. 2, created 03/27/2025, produced with eGRID R production model 1.0.2).
sources.notes: Table 1 (Subregion Output Emission Rates) and Table 3 (State Output Emission Rates) both carry an identical bottom "U.S." row; the national figures used here are taken from it. Rates are published in lb/MWh; this catalog stores g/kWh, converted with the exact NIST pound (0.45359237 kg) — see the factor notes for the arithmetic.
